speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I have noted your history of hypertension and will now conduct a physical exam and ask a few questions to identify the underlying cause in this pediatric patient.

First, how old are you, and when did you first notice symptoms like headaches, blurred vision, or swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. Since this is a well-child visit for a 5-year-old with newly noted hypertension and no family history, I need to determine if this is essential hypertension or secondary to an underlying condition.

REQUEST TEST: Basic_Metabolic_Panel (including sodium, potassium, creatinine) and Urinalysis.
REQUEST IMAGES: Renal_Ultrasound.

While those are being prepared, do you or your son notice any episodes of severe headaches, sweating, or palpitations?

speaker: Doctor
text: The basic metabolic panel and urinalysis results are normal, and the renal ultrasound images appear clear, which makes primary renal disease less likely. Given his age and the absence of family history, we should investigate for a primary adrenal cause or coarctation of the aorta. Have you noticed any recent episodes of high fever, weight loss, or abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Doctor
text: That finding of higher blood pressure in the right arm compared to the left is highly suggestive of a coarctation of the aorta, which restricts blood flow to the lower body. To confirm this suspicion, I need to perform a physical exam to listen for specific heart sounds and check for weak pulses in your son's legs. Can you describe how his legs feel or if he has had any leg pain or fatigue during play? REQUEST IMAGES: Echocardiogram.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Born full term with an uneventful neonatal period. Social history: Patient attends kindergarten. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco smoke.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming his normal social and developmental history. Since his blood pressure is higher in the right arm, we need to confirm if his lower extremity pulses are weak or absent compared to the upper extremities. Can you tell me if you have noticed any coolness or color change in his feet when he is playing?

speaker: Patient
text: All systems review is essentially negative as reported by the mother.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The negative review of systems, combined with the discrepancy in blood pressure between the right arm and the rest of the body, strongly points to a mechanical obstruction in the aorta. To confirm the diagnosis of Coarctation of the Aorta, I need to visualize the narrowing and check for weak pulses in the legs.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta
